ITQAN:v4p388/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p388/r22.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p388/r22.claim: The person whose heart is heedless is Uyayna ibn Hisn.
ITQAN:v4p388/r22.anchor: ﴿ من أغفلنا قلبه ﴾ هو عيينة بن حصن

BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.claim: The command means to restrain and steady oneself in the companions' company; morning and evening can mean constant supplication, or seeking success in the morning and pardon in the evening.
BURSEVI:v5p184/r1.anchor: احبسها وثبتها مصاحبة {مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغدواة والعشى}

BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.claim: Unbelieving chiefs demanded that Muhammad expel poor companions such as Suhayb, ʿAmmār, and Khabbāb, citing their smell and low status and promising mass conversion if he sat with elites; Noah's people made a similar complaint.
BURSEVI:v5p184/r2.anchor: نزلت حين طلب رؤساء الكفار طرد فقراء المسلمين من مجالسه عليه السلام كصهيب وعمار وخباب

BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.claim: Though expelling a few companions might seem a lesser harm than keeping the chiefs in disbelief, someone who refuses faith because of poor company is a hypocrite, so his demand deserves no regard.
BURSEVI:v5p184/r3.anchor: الإيمان حذرا من مجالسة الفقراء لم يكن إيمانه إيمانا بل يكون نفاقا قبيحا

BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.claim: Given the dignity of prophethood, expelling believers for an uncertain prospect would be grave wrongdoing; such exclusion belongs to worldly rulers, while religious leaders attend to inward states.
BURSEVI:v5p184/r4.anchor: يقول الفقير شان النبوة عظيم فلو طردهم لأجل أمر غير مقطوع كان ذنبا عظيما

BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.claim: Seeking God's Face means seeking His pleasure, not a worldly benefit; the metaphor connects approval to the face where approval and anger are manifest.
BURSEVI:v5p184/r5.anchor: أي : مريدين لرضاه لا شيء آخر من أعراض الدنيا فالوجه مجاز عن الرضى

BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r1.claim: Do not let your gaze pass beyond the poor companions; the eyes are the grammatical subject, while the command addresses their owner and warns against disdaining their worn clothing to seek the rich.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.speaker: ذو النون
BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.claim: He reads the verse as God's admonition to remain with those who stay at the divine presence morning and evening; those whose eyes never turn from God deserve that the Prophet never turn from them.
BURSEVI:v5p185/r2.anchor: وقال ذو النون رحمه الله خاطب الله نبيه عليه السلام وعاتبه

BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.speaker: زبدة التفاسير
BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.claim: It treats تريد as oriented to the future, not a judgment that the Prophet desired worldly adornment; he warned against worldly life and the rich. Al-Kashifi says he never desired it; the point is not to act that way.
BURSEVI:v5p185/r3.anchor: وفي "زبدة التفاسير" : تريد حال صرف للاستقبال

BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.claim: Do not obey those demanding the poor be removed; heedlessness prevents grasping realities, and God made the Quraysh chiefs heedless of remembrance.
BURSEVI:v5p185/r4.anchor: في تنحية الفقراء عن مجلسك {من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا}

BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185/r5.claim: Hawāʾ first means what the self loves and came to denote blameworthy desire opposed to religious law; an act is attributed to a servant by capacity and to God by creation.

BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.claim: The lexicon says farat can mean injustice, aggression, or an affair exceeding its limit; here the chiefs leave truth behind, like a horse ahead of the herd.
BURSEVI:v5p185/r6.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الفرط بضمتين الظلم والاعتداء والأمر المجاوز فيه عن الحد

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.claim: Following desire leads to ruin; the chiefs' opposition arose from heedless hearts occupied with fleeting falsehood, while honor lies in pure hearts and inner character, not outward beauty.
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r1.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : {وكان أمره} في متابعة الهوى هلاكا وخسرانا وفي الآية تنبيه على أن الباعث لهم

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.claim: His couplet says spiritual ascetics would not buy the satin robe of someone devoid of virtue.
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r2.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
قلندران حقيقت به نيم جو نخرند

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.claim: A hadith says God looks at hearts and deeds rather than forms and wealth; good hearts and acts bring acceptance regardless of appearance or riches.
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم وأموالكم بل إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم"

BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.claim: A story says angels questioned Abraham's suitability as intimate friend amid his attachments; God tested him through Gabriel, who offered to buy his twelve gold-collared dogs and flock. Abraham repeatedly let him take more, then gave all freely, refusing to revoke the gift when Gabriel disclosed himself. God directed him to sell them and endow the proceeds, which funded the shrine's endowment.
BURSEVI:v5p185#2/r4.anchor: روى أن الله تعالى لما اتخذ إبراهيم خليلا قالت الملائكة : يا رب

QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.claim: Patience with God’s people is steadfastness and empowered presence through God, with no attention turned elsewhere.
QASHANI:18:27-29/r3.anchor: أمر بالصبر مع الله وأهله وعدم الالتفات إلى غيره

QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.claim: Those invoking God morning and evening are stripped poor who seek only His essence, without worldly or afterlife needs or fixation on acts and attributes.
QASHANI:18:27-29/r4.anchor: هم الموحدون من الفقراء المجردين الذين لا يطلبون غير الله ولا حاجة لهم في الدنيا والآخرة

QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.claim: Morning and evening signify annihilation and abiding; looking away from these seekers means turning attention toward anything other than God.
QASHANI:18:27-29/r5.anchor: وقت احتجابها بهم عند البقاء، فالصبر معهم هو الصبر مع الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads al-ghudwah, treating the word as the named time without the ordinary article.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r2.claim: The other readers use al-ghadāh; the author considers this form clearer.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.claim: Although ghudwah is a proper name, it may be generalized and take the article; spelling it with wāw proves no wāw sound, as in الصلاة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p140/r3.anchor: أما غدوة فهو اسم موضوع للتعريف، وإذا كان كذلك

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī reads أغفلنا as 'We found him heedless,' not 'We made him heedless': if it expressed causation, the following consequence would normally use fa, not wa.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p139/r3.anchor: ولو كان أغفلنا هنا منقولا من غفل -أي: منعناه وصددناه-

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ولا تعد عينيك, a causative of 'your eyes passed beyond,' meaning turn your eyes away from the worldly adornment.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن: "ولا تعد عينيك9"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads من أغفلنا as 'one whom We found heedless,' not 'one whom We caused to be heedless'; the author defends this as an established أفعل usage and answers the theological objection.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p27/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عمرو بن فائد: "من أغفلنا قلبه2"

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r3.claim: The explanation of بالغداة والعشي is deferred to its discussion in al-Anʿām.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads بالغدوة with wāw; the other readers use بالغداة.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r3.anchor: ﴿ بالغداة والعشي ﴾ 28 قرأ ابن عامر وحده

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.speaker: باقي القراء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r4.claim: All other readers use بالغداة without the wāw form reported for Ibn ʿĀmir.

QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.claim: Ghudwa and ghadāt both mean morning, with the former emphasizing a single morning act and the latter a time period.
QIRAAT-ER:18:28:9#1/r1.anchor: ghudwa emphasizes the single morning act while ghadāt emphasizes the time period

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r2.claim: The command says to restrain the Prophet's self rather than his heart because his heart was already with God; outward conduct is directed publicly while the heart is reserved inwardly.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.claim: The phrase about seeking God's face functions as a circumstantial expression and signals that their morning and evening invocation and intention continue without interruption.
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r3.anchor: معناها مريدين وجهه أي في معنى الحال

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r4.claim: God sheltered these seekers in worldly life through His great gifts and in the afterlife through His generous gifts; He also disclosed their hidden qualities.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.claim: Once freed from suspicion, they became free of desire for and love of every created being.
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r5.anchor: لما زالت التهم سلمت لهم هذه الإرادة

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.claim: Out of reverence for the Prophet and the divine threshold, the poor did not press their request; he was told not to avert his gaze from them for worldly adornment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r6.anchor: لما تقاصر لسانهم عن السؤال هذه الجملة مراعاة منهم لهيبة الرسول

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.claim: The Prophet's gaze upon the poor companions serves as their means toward God and compensates them for not seeing Him until the afterlife.
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r7.anchor: جعلنا نظرك اليوم إليهم ذريعة لهم إلينا

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r8.claim: The heedless include people who asked the Prophet to clear his gathering of the poor; heedlessness also means being occupied with blessings instead of their Giver.

QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.claim: Negligence is spending time on something other than fulfilling an obligation or performing a voluntary act.
QUSHAYRI:v2p217/r9.anchor: الغفلة تزجية الوقت في غير قضاء فرض

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.speaker: عبد الرزاق
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.claim: Abd al-Razzaq links the command not to follow the heedless man who follows desire to Uyayna ibn Hisn.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r2.anchor: قال نا عبد الرزاق وأنزل في عيينة ﴿ ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه ﴾ إلى ﴿ فرطا ﴿

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.claim: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet praised God for making members of his community people with whom he was commanded to remain patient.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما نزلت ﴿ واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ﴾ قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الحمد لله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.claim: Ibrahim and Mujahid identify those who remember God morning and evening as the people of the five prayers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p401/r2.anchor: عن منصور عن إبراهيم ومجاهد في قوله ﴿ واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم ﴾ قال أهل الصلوات الخمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda consider the verse commanding patience with the worshippers a Medinan exception to the otherwise Meccan sura.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وقتادة إلا قوله واصبر نفسك الآية فمدنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.claim: One occasion report says Quraysh offered to sit with the Prophet if he dismissed poor followers such as ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Salmān, Ibn Masʿūd, and Bilāl, complaining about the smell of their clothes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r1.anchor: قال كفار قريش لو أبعدت هؤلاء عن نفسك لجالسناك وصحبناك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.speaker: سلمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.claim: Salmān reports that ʿUyayna b. Ḥiṣn, al-Aqraʿ, and other reconciled leaders made the request, which would make the verse Medinan; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the Quraysh report because the sura is Meccan and their behavior matched it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r2.anchor: وعن سلمان أن قائل ذلك عيينة بن حصين والأقرع وذووهم من المؤلفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r3.claim: اصبر نفسك means keep yourself with them and remain steadfast; the command shows special care for these companions, with مع requiring companionship and shared company.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s verse about a noble woman holding steady while a coward’s breath rises illustrates the sense of صبرت as enduring steadfastly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r4.anchor: فصبرت عارفة لذلك حرة ... ترسو إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.claim: A prophetic report forbids ṣabr of an animal, meaning tying it up as a target for shooting; this shows the word’s sense of restraint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث النهي عن صبر الحيوان أي حبسه للرمي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, and Ibrāhīm take morning and evening as the five daily prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم: بالغداة والعشي إشارة إلى الصلوات الخمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.claim: Qatāda specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: إلى صلاة الفجر وصلاة العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.claim: He also allows the phrase to mean constant worship generally, as ‘striking front and back’ can refer to the whole body rather than only those parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p166/r8.anchor: وقد يقال: إن ذلك يراد به العموم أي يدعون ربهم دائما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.claim: Where ordinary wording supports the meaning, Abū Ḥayyān prefers its lexical sense over an added semantic incorporation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r1.anchor: أما إذا أمكن إجراء اللفظ على مدلوله الوضعي فإنه يكون أولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ likewise treats the doubled form as transitive, as with the hamzated reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r2.anchor: وكذا قال صاحب اللوامح. قال: وهذا مما عديته بالتضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Basran grammarians accept this kind of semantic incorporation only under necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r3.anchor: البصريين وإنما يذهب إليه عند الضرورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ولا تعد from the hamzated form أعدى; another report from him, ʿĪsā, and al-Aʿmash has doubled ʿayn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: ولا تعد من أعدى، وعنه أيضا وعن عيسى والأعمش ولا تعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and the author of al-Lawāmiʿ claim hamza or doubling makes the verb transitive, citing the verse فعد عما ترى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نقلا بالهمزة وبنقل الحشو ومنه قوله: فعد عما ترى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.claim: He rejects that analysis: hamza and doubling here do not add transitivity, since the base verb is already transitive and only one object appears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r6.anchor: بل الهمزة والتكثير في هذه الكلمة ليسا للتعدية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا as a circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.claim: If the possessor is the dual عيناك, the verb should be تريدان; if it is the Prophet, a circumstance attached to a genitive pronoun has a syntactic difficulty, though some allow it when the possessed noun is part-like. The eyes stand for the Prophet’s looking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r8.anchor: إن قدر عيناك فكان يكون التركيب تريدان، وإن قدر الكاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives Muʿtazilī readings of من أغفلنا قلبه: God made or found the heart heedless, or left it unmarked by remembrance like an unbranded animal or unvowelled book; he also links this to hearts not given faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r9.anchor: من أغفلنا قلبه من جعلنا قلبه غافلا عن الذكر بالخذلان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.speaker: الرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.claim: The Muʿtazilī al-Rummānī says God did not mark the heart with the signs given to believers, likening it to an unbranded camel or unvowelled book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r10.anchor: والتأويل الآخر تأويل الرماني وكان معتزليا قال: لم نسمه بما نسم به قلوب المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān contrasts Sunnī teaching: God truly made the person heedless and creates the misguidance and heedlessness within him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r11.anchor: وأما أهل السنة فيقولون: إن الله تعالى أغفله حقيقة وهو خالق الضلال فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.speaker: المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal glosses أغفلنا as leaving the person empty of remembrance, meaning the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p167/r12.anchor: وقال المفضل: أخليناه عن الذكر وهو القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r1.claim: The people whose hearts were made heedless are apparently Quraysh, whose disbelief and prevailing wretchedness occupied their hearts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.claim: He prefers Quraysh over the proposed identifications with ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ because the verse is Meccan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r2.anchor: عيينة والأقرع والأول أولى لأن الآية مكية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.speaker: عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.claim: They read aghfalnā with the lām open and qalbahu with the bāʾ damma, syntactically assigning the action to the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r3.anchor: قرأ عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد أغفلنا بفتح اللام قلبه بضم الباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.speaker: ابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the variant as meaning that God found them heedless of the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r4.anchor: قال ابن جني من ظننا غافلين عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses the variant as finding the heart heedless, from the verb meaning to find someone heedless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r5.anchor: حسبنا قلبه غافلين من أغفلته إذا وجدته غافلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.claim: They interpret faratan as loss and waste.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r6.anchor: وكان أمره فرطا. قال قتادة ومجاهد: ضياعا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān reads faratan as excess or extravagance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: سرفا. وقال الفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ understands faratan as abandoned or neglected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses faratan as going beyond the proper limit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.claim: Ibn Baḥr takes faratan as something immediate and swift, citing the description of man as hasty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r10.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: الفرط العاجل السريع، كما قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.claim: Other transmitted glosses of faratan are regret and falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r11.anchor: وقيل: ندما. وقيل: باطلا. وقال ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets faratan as opposed to the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: مخالفا للحق. وقال ابن عطية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows faratan to mean either neglecting what one should keep to or excess and extravagance in one's course and desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p168/r13.anchor: الفرط يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى التفريط والتضييع، أي أمره

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.claim: God commanded the wealthy to sit patiently with the poor and follow their way.
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r1.anchor: قال ذو النون رحمه الله : أمر الله تعالى الأغنياء بمجالسة الفقراء والصبر معهم والاستنان بسنتهم

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.speaker: عمرو المكي
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.claim: Companionship with righteous, truthful poor people is a path to paradise, moving between contentment and certainty.
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r2.anchor: قال عمرو المكي : صحبة الصالحين والفقراء الصادقين عين أهل الجنة يتقلب من الرضا إلى اليقين

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم بن شيبان
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.claim: The chivalry of people of gnosis is enduring patience within the fortress of necessity alongside the patient.
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r3.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن شيبان : فتوة أهل المعرفة دوام الاصطبار في حصن الاضطرار مع أهل الصبر

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is told to remain with those who endure for God with self, heart, and spirit, who never leave the special divine presence; God likewise remains with them.
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : خاطب الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وعاتبه أنبه وقال له : اصبر على من صبر علينا بنفسه

SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.claim: Do not look away from them toward others, because their eyes never turn away from God.
SULAMI:v1p409#2/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي لا تعد عيناك عنهم إلى غيرهم فإنهم لا تعدو أعينهم مني طرفة عين

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.claim: There is beneficial heedlessness, a mercy that permits life and bodily rest, and punitive heedlessness, forgetting God and neglecting awareness that He watches.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : الغفلة غفلتان : غفلة نعمة ، وغفلة عقوبة

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.claim: Heedlessness is neglecting what one was commanded and forgetting God's continual blessings.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r2.anchor: وسئل أبو عثمان : عن الغفلة ؟ فقال : إهمال ما أمرت به ونسيان تواتر نعم الله عندك

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.claim: Heedlessness is following the lower self's desires.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الغفلة متابعة النفس على ما تشتهيها

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r4.claim: Heedlessness is the heart's punishment and its veil from the Benefactor.

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r5.speaker: الجوزجاني
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r5.anchor: وقال الجوزجاني : الغفلة هي طول الأمل

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.speaker: النوري
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.claim: Heedlessness is the inner secret settling in anything other than the Real.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r6.anchor: وقال النوري : الغفلة سكون السر إلى شيء سوى الحق

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.speaker: ابن الجلاء
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.claim: Heedlessness is what makes a person lapse into slackness.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الجلاء : الغفلة ما يورثك الفترة

SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.claim: Heedlessness is wasting time in idleness.
SULAMI:v1p409#5/r8.anchor: وقال سهل : الغفلة : إبطال الوقت بالبطالة

TUSTARI:18:28/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r1.claim: Heedlessness is wasting one’s time in idleness.

TUSTARI:18:28/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r2.claim: The heart has a thousand deaths, culminating in separation from God, and a thousand lives, culminating in meeting the Real.
TUSTARI:18:28/r2.anchor: إن للقلب ألف موت، آخرها القطيعة عن الله عز وجل، وإن للقلب ألف حياة، آخرها لقاء الحق عز وجل

TUSTARI:18:28/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:28/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:28/r3.claim: Every sin brings death to the heart, and every act of obedience brings it life.
TUSTARI:18:28/r3.anchor: وإن في كل معصية للقلب موتا، وفي كل طاعة للقلب حياة

AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.claim: ولا تعد عيناك uses the dual sense: your two eyes should not turn away from them.
AKHFASH:v2p430/r1.anchor: وقال {ولا تعد عيناك عنهم} أي: العينان فلا تعدوان.

FARRA:v2p139/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p139/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
FARRA:v2p139/r3.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami alone is known to have read بالغدوة; Arabic normally treats غدوة as definite without ال, as in a report meaning this morning.
FARRA:v2p139/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي (بالغدوة والعشي) ولا أعلم أحدا قرأ غيره

FARRA:v2p139/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p139/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p139/r4.claim: ولا تعد عيناك makes the two eyes the subject: do not let your eyes turn away from the believers; the verse was revealed about Salman and his companions.
FARRA:v2p139/r4.anchor: الفعل للعينين: لا تنصرف عيناك عنهم. وهذه نزلت في سلمان وأصحابه

FARRA:v2p140/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p140/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p140/r1.claim: فرطا means abandoned and neglected obedience; another account says Uyayna ibn Hisn exceeded in speech by claiming leadership and nobility.
FARRA:v2p140/r1.anchor: (وكان أمره فرطا) متروكا قد ترك فيه الطاعة وغفل عنها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.claim: Do not let your eyes pass beyond the poor companions to worldly adornment.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r1.anchor: {ولا تعد عيناك عنهم} أي لا تتجاوزهم إلى زينة الحياة الدنيا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets faraṭ as regret; other interpreters say excess, with the root meaning haste and precedence.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#5/r2.anchor: {وكان أمره فرطا} أي ندما. [هذا] قول أبي عبيدة: وقول المفسرين: سرفا.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.claim: “Restrain yourself” means hold someone in place, as in the prohibition against confining an animal for target practice; applying it to steadfast endurance is an extended use, not the literal sense, because the verb's transitivity differs.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r1.anchor: أي احبسها وثبتها يقال صبرت زيدا أي حبسته وفي الحديث النهي عن صبر الحيوان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.claim: Being with the people means keeping their company; calling upon God morning and evening is a common way to express constant worship, like saying someone struck morning and evening to mean the whole body.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r2.anchor: ( أي مصاحبة مع الذين ( يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ( أي يعبدونه دائما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.claim: Some keep morning and evening literal rather than treating them as all times; these times are singled out because people are distracted by work and are prone to heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r3.anchor: وأبقى غير واحد الغداة والعشي على ظاهر هما ولم يرد عموم الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.claim: The worship in question is remembrance of God, reported from Ibrāhīm through Mughīra.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r4.anchor: قيل ذكر الله تعالى وروي ذلك من طريق مغيرة عن إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.speaker: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.claim: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār is reported to say the worship is recitation of the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : قراءة القرآن وروي ذلك عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr says it means discussing lawful and unlawful matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج الحكيم الترمذي عن ابن جبير أن المراد بها المفاوضة والحلال والحرام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Mujāhid identify the worship as attending the five daily prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عمر ومجاهد هي شهود الصلوات الخمس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.claim: Qatāda specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers; al-Ālūsī says the preceding discussion supports the apparent, literal times.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r8.anchor: وعن قتادة شهود صلاة الصبح والعصر وفيما تقدم ما يؤيد ظاهره أولها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.claim: The people meant are poor Companions, including ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Salmān, Ibn Masʿūd, and Bilāl.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بالموصول فقراء الصحابة عمار وصهيب وسلمان وابن مسعود وبلال وأضرابهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.claim: One reported occasion is that Quraysh chiefs, including Umayya ibn Khalaf, offered to listen if the Prophet moved poor believers away because their wool garments smelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r10.anchor: قال كفار قريش كأمية بن خلف وغيره من صناديد أهل مكة لو أبعدت هؤلاء عن نفسك لجالسناك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.speaker: سلمان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.claim: A report from Salmān says the influential converts ʿUyayna ibn Badr and al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis asked the Prophet to sit at the head of the assembly and send away Salmān, Abū Dharr, and the poor Muslims in wool garments so they could listen and learn.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r11.anchor: عن سلمان قال : جاءت المؤلفة قلوبهم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عيينة بن بدر والأقرع بن حابس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.claim: The reports disagree about the verse's setting: the Quraysh account makes it Meccan, while the Salmān report makes it Medinan; Abū Ḥayyān prefers Meccan because the surah is Meccan, but al-Ālūsī says most reports support Medina and such verses can be exceptions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r12.anchor: والآية على هذا مدنية وعلى الأول مكية قال أبو حيان : وهو أصح لأن السورة مكية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.claim: A report through Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk attributes the Meccan occasion to Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Ālūsī says the verses that follow may favor the Medinan setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r13.anchor: وقد أخرج ما يؤيد الأول ابن مردويه من طريق جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.claim: The relative description “those who call their Lord” explains the order to remain with them: their defining devotion warrants continued companionship.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r14.anchor: والتعبير عن أولئك بالموصول لتعليل الأمر بما في حيز الصلة من الخصلة الداعية إلى إدامة الصحبة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads “in the morning” with the definite article. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl explain this through Arabs' use of the word as an indefinite noun; al-Raḍī says it can be indefinite by agreement, although it is usually a declinable-proper genus name.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( بالغدوة ( وخرج ذلك على ما ذكره سيبويه والخليل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.claim: Some verifiers prefer the first grammatical explanation because making a genus name indefinite is less clear than making a personal proper name indefinite; al-Fannārī objects to treating the month name Rajab this way, and al-Ālūsī leaves the discussion to its proper place.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r16.anchor: واختار بعض المحققين التخريج الأول وقال : إنه أحسن دراية ورواية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.claim: This verse is more emphatic than the parallel command not to drive away those who call upon God morning and evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r17.anchor: وهذه الآية كما في البحر أبلغ من التي في الأنعام وهي قوله تعالى : ( ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.speaker: السهيلي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.claim: “Seeking God's face” means seeking His pleasure and approved obedience, not display or fame; al-Suhaylī explains the metaphor through the turning toward someone one favors and turning away from someone one resents.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r18.anchor: بناء على ما قاله الإمام السهيلي من أن الوجه إذا أضيف إليه تعالى يراد به الرضا والطاعة المرضية مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.claim: Alternative readings take “face” as God's essence with an omitted genitive, or as turning toward Him and seeking nearness; al-Ālūsī prefers the first, pleasure-based interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261#2/r19.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالوجه الذات والكلام على حذف مضاف وقيل : هو بمعنى التوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.claim: The command forbids turning attention from the poor believers toward worldly people; its purpose is to prevent scorning them for their shabby condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r1.anchor: والمراد النهي عن احتقارهم وصرف النظر عنهم لرثاثة حالهم إلى غيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.claim: He reads عدا as “turn away,” with the verb taking the person or thing turned from as its second complement through عن.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r2.anchor: عداه عن الأمر عدوا وعدوانا صرفه واختار هذا أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.claim: An alternative lexical construction gives عدا one object with عن, meaning to pass over or leave something.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r3.anchor: عدا الأمر وعنه جاوزه وتركه وجوز أن يكون معنى الآية على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.claim: Raghib says عدا intrinsically means passing beyond; Zamakhshari therefore supplies the sense of recoiling or rising above the object to explain عن.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r4.anchor: إن عدا حقيقة معناه تجاوز كما صرح به الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.claim: Zamakhshari argues that the wording combines leaving the believers and recoiling from them, a stronger effect than a single sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r5.anchor: ارتكب التضمين ليعطى الكلام مجموع معنيين وذلك أقوى من إعطاء معنى فذ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that Arabic-style verb inclusion is not analogical and should be used only from necessity when the ordinary lexical sense works.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r6.anchor: بأن التضمين لا ينقاس عند البصريين وإنما يذهب إليه عند الضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.claim: The further objection that a semantic synonym must share the same transitivity is not compelling; the lexicon supports the alternative reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r7.anchor: لا يلزم من اتحاد الفعلين في المعنى اتحادهما في التعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb lightly as أعداه, with the eyes as an accusative object.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r8.anchor: بضم التاء وسكون العين وكسر الدال المخففة من أعداه ونصب العينين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.speaker: عيسى والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.claim: Isa and al-Aʿmash read the doubled verb عَدَّاهُ, likewise with the eyes in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r9.anchor: بضم التاء وفتح العين وتشديد الدال المكسورة من عداه يعديه ونصب العينين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.speaker: الزمخشري وصاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.claim: They treat the hamza and doubling in these readings as causative morphology.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r10.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري وصاحب اللوامح الهمزة والتضعيف للتعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan says that analysis fails: since the base verb already takes an object, causative morphology should yield two objects, which these readings lack.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263/r11.anchor: بل الهمزة والتضعيف في هذه الكلمة لموافقة أفعل وفعل للفعل المجرد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.claim: “Seeking worldly adornment” means seeking the company of wealthy worldly people unlike the poor believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r1.anchor: أي تطلب مجالسة من لم يكن مثلهم من الأغنياء وأصحاب الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.claim: On the canonical reading the clause is circumstantial, most naturally attached to the eyes in عيناك; the genitive relation can license that attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r2.anchor: وجازت الحال منه لأنه جزء المضاف إليه والعامل على ما قيل معنى الإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashf assigns the circumstantial clause to the preceding verb, as in the construction بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r3.anchor: وقال في الكشف : العامل الفعل السابق كما تقرر في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.claim: The singular “you seek” can be attributed to the eye as a metonym for its owner’s desire; it may also mean looking for play rather than reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r4.anchor: بأن إرادتها كناية عن إرادة صاحبها ألا ترى إلى ما شاع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.claim: The eye is treated as singular because perception is one, to signal its rhetorical insertion, or because the paired eyes are one bodily organ.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r5.anchor: إما لاتحاد الإحساس أو للتنبيه على مكان الإقحام أو للإكتفاء بأحدهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.claim: The author finds the ordinary circumstantial reading sound under either explanation of تعد; objections to a circumstantial clause from a genitive are too weak to displace it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن نية عدو لا عن الظاهر من غير داع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.claim: Some assign the clause to the genitive only when تعد means passing beyond, and to the governing noun when it means turning away; the author sees this as stylistic preference.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r7.anchor: خص بعضهم كونها حالا من المضاف إليه على التقدير الأول وكونها حالا من المضاف على التقدير الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.claim: If turning away is meant, attaching desire to the eye keeps the sentence’s beginning and end parallel and avoids directly attributing worldly desire to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r8.anchor: فناسب إسناد الارادة إليها في آخره ليكون أول الكلام وآخره على طرز واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.claim: On the two anomalous readings, the clause is circumstantial from the hidden subject of the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r9.anchor: وهي على القراءتين الشاذتين حال من فاعل الفعل المستتر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.claim: “Do not obey” prohibits removing the poor from the Prophet’s gathering at the urging of the heedless elite.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r10.anchor: ولا تطع ( في تنحية الفقراء عن مجلسك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.claim: God made the elite’s hearts wholly unprepared for remembrance; their heedlessness contrasts with the poor who invoke God morning and evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r11.anchor: لبطلان استعداده للذكر بالمرة كأولئك الذين يدعونك إلى طرد الفقراء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.speaker: المفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.claim: Al-Mufaddal interprets remembrance here as the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p263#2/r12.anchor: ومعنى الذكر ظاهر وفسره المفضل بالقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.claim: The verse’s apparent wording supports the Sunni doctrine that God makes the heart heedless; Muʿtazilites reinterpret it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r1.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في مذهب أهل السنة وأولها المعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.claim: The well-known Muʿtazilite interpretation takes “We made his heart heedless” as God’s abandonment or withdrawal of aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r2.anchor: فقيل المراد أغفلنا قلبه بالخذلان وهذا هو التأويل المشهور عندهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.claim: Interpreting the phrase as “We found him heedless” is objectionable because it suggests God stumbled upon the state without prior knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا ينبغي أن يتجرأ على تفسير فعل أسنده الله تعالى إليه بالمصادفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.speaker: الكميت
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the verb as “attributed heedlessness to him,” illustrated by al-Kumayt’s line about people calling him wrong or sinful.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r4.anchor: قول الكميت : وطائفة قد أكفروني بحبكم وطائفة قالوا مسيء ومذنب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.speaker: الرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.claim: Al-Rummani says God did not mark the heart with remembrance as a sign of faith, using the image of an unmarked animal; the author calls it subtle but contrary to the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r5.anchor: المراد لم نسم قلبه بالذكر ولم نجعله من القلوب التي كتبنا في الايمان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.claim: They argue that “he followed his desire” assigns the act to the servant, and that a divinely caused sequence should have used a causal فَـ.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r6.anchor: حيث أسند اتباع الهوى إلى العبد فيدل على أنه فعله لا فعل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.claim: Human acts may be attributed to the servant through acquisition and power and to God through creation; omission of a causal particle can be rhetorically deliberate.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r7.anchor: يجوز إسناده إليه بالاعتبار الأول وإلى الله تعالى بالثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.speaker: عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.claim: They read أَغْفَلْنَا with fatḥa on ف and ل and قلبه nominative, making the heart the subject: “we found it heedless.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r8.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن فائد وموسى الأسواري وعمرو بن عبيد ( أغفلنا ) بفتح الفاء واللام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.claim: On that reading, the sense is that God supposed them heedless, with remembrance of God used as a metonym for divine requital.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r9.anchor: والمراد ظننا وحسبنا غافلين عن ذكرنا له ولصنيعه بالمؤاخذة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.claim: An objection says removing the poor might secure elite conversion, making a small injury preferable to the greater harm of continued unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r10.anchor: وفي عدم طردهم لزم ترتب ضرر عظيم وهو بقاء أولئك الكفرة على كفرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.claim: God knew the elite would at most make a merely outward profession, insufficient reason to violate the honor of the righteous poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p264/r11.anchor: علم أن أولئك الكفرة لا يؤمنون إيمانا حقيقيا بل إن يؤمنوا إيمانا ظاهريا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.claim: God may also have forbidden expulsion because humiliating early believers would alienate hearts, prompt recent converts to apostatize, and deter future entrants.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r1.anchor: فربما يرتد من هو قريب عهد بإسلام ويقل الداخلون في دينه بعد ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.claim: This potential damage to Islam outweighs leaving a small group of unbelievers in their disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r2.anchor: وذلك ضرر عظيم فوق ضرر بقاء شرذمة من الكفار على الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r3.claim: Mujahid explains فرطا as waste and ruin.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes فرطا as having advanced past truth and right, leaving them behind.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r4.anchor: متقدما على الحق والصواب نابذا له وراء ظهره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows فرطا to mean either neglect and waste of religion or excess and extravagance; Muqatil likewise glosses it as extravagance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون الفرط بمعنى التفريط والتضييع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r6.claim: Muqatil explains the word as excess and extravagance.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.claim: Calling the elite “those whose hearts We made heedless” signals that their heedlessness and appetite explain why they must not be obeyed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p265/r7.anchor: للإيذان بعلية ما فيه حيز الصلة للنهي عن الإطاعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.claim: The verse was revealed when ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, before accepting Islam, asked the Prophet to dismiss poor companions such as Salman or give elites a separate gathering, promising mass conversion if he did.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r8.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {واصبر نفسك} الآية نزلت في عيينة بن حصن الفزاري أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يسلم وعنده جماعة من الفقراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.claim: The Prophet must stay with those who call on God morning and evening seeking Him alone, not worldly gain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r9.anchor: أي: احبس يا محمد نفسك {مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} طرفي النهار {يريدون وجهه} أي: يريدون الله لا يريدون به عرضا من الدنيا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.claim: He says the verse concerned the seven hundred poor Companions of the Bench, who lived in the mosque without trade or farmland and spent their days in prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في أصحاب الصفة وكانوا سبعمائة رجل فقراء في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يرجعون إلى تجارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.claim: The Prophet praised God for placing in his community people with whom he was commanded to remain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166/r11.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الحمد لله الذي جعل في أمتي من أمرت أن أصبر نفسي معهم "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.claim: Do not turn your eyes from poor companions toward the wealthy and eminent in pursuit of worldly adornment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r1.anchor: {ولا تعد} أي: لا تصرف ولا تتجاوز {عيناك عنهم} إلى غيرهم {تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.claim: God made the heart of the heedless person inattentive to remembrance; the person is identified as ʿUyayna or, by another view, Umayya ibn Khalaf.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r2.anchor: {ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا} أي: جعلنا قلبه غافلا عن ذكرنا يعني: عيينة بن حصن. وقيل: أمية بن خلف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r3.claim: They interpret faratan as loss or waste.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل ابن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r4.claim: He interprets it as excess or extravagance.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.claim: He interprets it as going beyond the proper limit; Baghawī relates this to ʿUyayna's excessive claim that all people would convert if their leaders did.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش: مجاوزا للحد (2) . قيل: معنى التجاوز في الحد هو قول عيينة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.claim: Other glosses are wasting one's affairs and days, regret, falsehood, or opposition to the truth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p166#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه ضيع أمره (1) وعطل أيامه وقيل: ندما

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.claim: The command is to hold oneself firmly with those who invoke God at the gathering times or at the day's two ends; Ibn Amir reads the form as al-ghudwa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r1.anchor: في مجامع أوقاتهم، أو في طرفي النهار

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r2.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking His approval and obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.claim: Do not let your gaze pass over the poor believers, turning away from their shabby clothes in desire for wealthy people's finery; the construction embeds the sense of turning away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r3.anchor: ولا يجاوزهم نظرك إلى غيرهم، وتعديته بعن

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.claim: The phrase is also read with the dual eyes or with a form derived from causing the eye to pass beyond them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r4.anchor: وقرىء «ولا تعد عينيك» { ولا تعد } من أعداه وعداه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.claim: The person whose heart was made heedless is identified as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who urged Muhammad to expel poor believers for Quraysh's leaders.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r5.anchor: كأمية بن خلف في دعائك إلى طرد الفقراء عن مجلسك

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.claim: Mu'tazilites reject the apparent divine attribution of heedlessness, suggesting God found the heart so, attributed it to the person, or left it unmarked; the author answers with his previous arguments.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r6.anchor: والمعتزلة لما غاظهم إسناد الإغفال إلى الله تعالى قالوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.claim: Following desire means the person's affair is excessive, advancing past truth and casting it behind his back; the root also describes a horse that runs ahead.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:28/r7.anchor: أي تقدما على الحق ونبذا له وراء ظهره

NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.speaker: نصر بن عاصم ومالك بن دينار وأبو عبد الرحمن
NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.claim: They read ‘do not drive away those who call on their Lord’ with ghudwata; their evidence is the written wāw.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r10.anchor: نصر بن عاصم ومالك بن دينار وأبو عبد الرحمن ' ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغدوة والعشي يريدون وجهه

NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.claim: The orthographic wāw does not prove this reading because ṣalāt and ḥayāt are also written with wāw; al-ghudwa is normally indefinite and does not take the article.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r11.anchor: وهذا لا يلزم لكتبهم الصلاة والحياة بالواو ، ولا تكاد العرب تقول : الغدوة لأنها معرفة ولا تدخل الألف واللام على معرفة

NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.claim: He reads ‘do not let your eyes overlook’ with naṣb because the verb governs it.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r12.anchor: وروي عن الحسن ^ ( لا تعد عينيك ) ^ نصب بوقوع الفعل عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.claim: The Prophet was grieving over unbelievers, while leaders offered to listen if he expelled poor believers such as Ammar, Suhaib, and Bilal.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r5.anchor: لو طردت هؤلاء الفقراء وأبعدتهم عنك مثل عمار وصهيب وبلال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.claim: He must remain with believers who call on God morning and evening seeking His face alone, even if they are socially poor.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r6.anchor: يريدون } أي بذلك { وجهه } لا غير ذلك في رجاء ثواب أو خوف عقاب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.claim: He must not turn toward worldly adornment or obey those whom God has made heedless, who follow desire and exceed all bounds.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r7.anchor: هوه } بالميل إلى ما استدرجناه به منها والأنفة من مجالسة أوليائنا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.claim: The author reads أغفلنا as God's action: He caused the heart to be heedless, and the consequent loss of remembrance leaves darkness for desire to fill.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r8.anchor: ولما كان التقدير : فغفل , لأن عظمتنا لا يغلبها شيء فلا يكون إلا ما نريد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.claim: The followers will be rescued and raised over tyrants as the cave sleepers were, because they turn to God and away from everything else.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p462/r9.anchor: سينجي أتباعك على ضعفهم منهم كما أنجى أصحاب الكهف , ويزيدك بأن يعليهم عليهم

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.claim: Influential men asked the Prophet to exclude poor Muslims such as Salman and Abu Dharr and seat the chiefs instead; revelation of the passage threatened them with Hell.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r10.anchor: عن سلمان قال: جاءت المؤلفة قلوبهم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: عيينة بن بدر والأقرع بن حابس

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.claim: The Prophet searched for the poor worshippers in the back of the mosque, found them remembering God, and praised God for commanding him to remain with them in life and death.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r1.anchor: عن سلمان قال: قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يلتمسهم حتى أصابهم في مؤخر المسجد يذكرون الله

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.claim: A man wearing a coarse cloak shoved Salman aside and asked the Prophet to keep the poor away when elites visited; the verse commanding patience with them was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r2.anchor: عن سلمان قال: نزلت هذه الآية في وفي رجل دخل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم - ومعي شن خوص -

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.claim: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet found ragged, humble people remembering God, sat with them, and praised God for including them in his community.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف قال: نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بعض أبياته

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة وأبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.claim: When a man read al-Hijr and al-Kahf, the Prophet identified the gathering as the one in which he was commanded to remain.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r4.anchor: عن بي هريرة وأبي سعيد قالا: جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل يقرأ سورة الحجر وسورة الكهف

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.speaker: عمر بن ذر
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.claim: When Abdullah ibn Rawaha stopped reminding his companions upon the Prophet's arrival, the Prophet told him to continue and called them the gathering with whom he was ordered to remain.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r5.anchor: من طريق عمر بن ذر عن أبيه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهى إلى نفر من أصحابه

DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.claim: Mujahid transmits Ibn Abbas's report of the Prophet telling Abdullah ibn Rawaha that his companions were the assembly God commanded him to remain with.
DURR-FULL:v5p380/r6.anchor: من طريق عمر بن ذر: حدثني مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: مر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.claim: A report continues that angels attend gatherings where God is remembered, mirror the worshippers' praise, then God forgives the group, including a sinful companion, since no one sitting with them is deprived.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r1.anchor: إنه ما جلس عدتكم إلا جلس معه عدتهم جليسهم من الملائكة إن سبحوا الله سبحوه

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.claim: The Prophet asked a preacher to continue; sitting in the morning until sunrise, he said, was dearer than freeing four slaves.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على قاص يقص فأمسك فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قص

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.claim: The Prophet told poor Muslims with a Quran reciter to rejoice in complete light on Judgment Day and enter Paradise five hundred years before the wealthy, who will be reckoned.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: أتى علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ونحن ناس من ضعفة المسلمين ورجل يقرأ علينا القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.speaker: ثابت
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.claim: When Salman and others stopped remembering God as the Prophet approached, he asked them to continue, saying he had seen mercy descend and wanted to share it.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r4.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان سلمان في عصابة يذكرون الله فمر النبي فكفوا فقال: ما كنتم تقولون

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.claim: A heavenly caller announces forgiveness and the replacement of sins with good deeds for people who gather solely to remember God.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r5.anchor: عن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما من قوم اجتمعوا يذكرون الله لا يريدون بذلك إلا وجهه

DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.claim: Ibn Umar says those addressed by the command to remain with worshippers are people who attend the obligatory prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p381/r6.anchor: عن نافع قال: أخبرني عبد الله بن عمر في هذه الآية {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم} أنهم الذين يشهدون الصلوات المكتوبة

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the people of remembrance as worshippers who attend the obligatory prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.claim: The verse refers to the dawn and afternoon prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r2.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده في قوله: {واصبر نفسك} الآية قال: نزلت في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.speaker: عبيد الله بن عدي بن الخيار
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.claim: The people with whom the Prophet should remain are Quran reciters.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r3.anchor: عن عبيد الله بن عدي بن الخيار في هذه الآية قال: هم الذين يقرأون القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command not to obey the heedless was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf's demand that the poor be dismissed and Meccan chiefs brought near; heedlessness means a heart sealed against monotheism, and following desire means idolatry.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا} قال: نزلت في أمية بن خلف

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.speaker: ابن بريدة
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.claim: Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to exclude Salman because of the smell of his wool garment when elites visited; the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r5.anchor: عن ابن بريدة قال: دخل عيينة بن حصن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في يوم حار وعنده سلمان

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.claim: Al-Rabi says the Prophet turned from distracted Umayya ibn Khalaf after the verse was revealed, then found Salman remembering God and praised those he was commanded to remain with.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r6.anchor: عن الربيع قال: حدثنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تصدى لأمية بن خلف وهو ساه غافل

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.claim: Ibrahim identifies the morning and evening worshippers as people of remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم في قوله: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} قال: هم أهل الذكر

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.claim: Ibrahim says not to drive the worshippers away from remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم في قوله: {واصبر نفسك} الآية قال: لا تطردهم عن الذكر

DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.claim: The Prophet was commanded to stay with his companions and teach them the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v5p382/r9.anchor: عن أبي جعفر في الآية قال: أمر أن يصبر نفسه مع أصحابه يعلمهم القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says those who call upon their Lord are those who worship Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {مع الذين يدعون ربهم} قال: يعبدون ربهم

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.claim: The instruction not to let one's eyes pass beyond them means not to look away from them toward others.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r2.anchor: قوله: {ولا تعد عيناك عنهم} يقول: لا تتعداهم إلى غيرهم

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.speaker: أبو هاشم
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.claim: Abu Hashim says they would compare or distinguish one another regarding lawful and unlawful matters.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r3.anchor: عن أبي هاشم في الآية قال: كانوا يتفاضلون في الحلال والحرام

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr also connects the verse with distinctions concerning lawful and unlawful matters.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} قال: المفاضلة في الحلال والحرام

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.claim: Ibrahim and Mujahid identify the worshippers as those who perform the five daily prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم ومجاهد {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} قال: الصلوات الخمس

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed after Uyayna ibn Hisn asked for a separate gathering because Salman smelled bad to him.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: نزلت {ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا} في عيينة بن حصن

DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses فرطا as loss or waste.
DURR-FULL:v5p383/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وكان أمره فرطا} قال: ضياعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.claim: Meccan leaders said they would listen if poor believers and slaves were removed; God answered this demand at 6:52 and more forcefully here by ordering the Prophet to stay with them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r1.anchor: أن سادة المشركين كانوا زعموا أنه لولا أن من المؤمنين ناسا أهل خصاصة في الدنيا وأرقاء لا يدانوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.claim: Iṣbir nafsaka means keep yourself continually with them; ṣabr conveys staying fixed, and the verb takes maʿa because it includes the sense of companionship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r2.anchor: وما هنا آكد إذ أمره بملازمتهم بقوله : واصبر نفسك } ، أي احبسها معهم حبس ملازمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.claim: Al-ghadāh is the time between dawn and sunrise, and al-ʿashī is evening; their prayer and supplication encompass the day and night, including formal prayers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r3.anchor: و { الغداة } قرأه الجمهور بألف بعد الدال : اسم الوقت الذي بين الفجر وطلوع الشمس . والعشي : المساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads bil-ghudwah with sukūn on dāl and a wāw, a synonym of al-ghadāh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { بالغدوة } بسكون الدال وواو بعد الدال مفتوحة وهو مرادف الغداة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.claim: Calling them ‘those who pray’ hints that their devotion makes them especially worthy of companionship; ‘seeking His face’ figuratively means seeking God’s favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r5.anchor: والتعبير عنهم بالموصول للإيماء إلى تعليل الأمر بملازمتهم ، أي لأنهم أحرياء بذلك لأجل إقبالهم على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p304#2/r6.claim: The apparent command not to let the eyes pass them means not to look away or ignore them; addressing the eyes themselves is an elegant compression for addressing their owner.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.claim: ‘Wanting worldly adornment’ describes the addressee’s state; desire for status or appearance must not cause him to leave companions lacking outward finery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r1.anchor: وجملة { تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا } حال من كاف الخطاب ، لأن المضاف جزء من المضاف إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.claim: The verse exposes the elites’ foolish fixation on appearances and their contempt for people of virtue, sound minds, and enlightened hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p305/r2.anchor: وهذا الكلام تعريض بحماقة سادة المشركين الذين جعلوا همهم وعنايتهم بالأمور الظاهرة وأهملوا الاعتبار بالحقائق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.claim: The prohibition establishes a broad rule for the Prophet and Muslims in responding to polytheists’ demands and ends their hope of obtaining concessions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r1.anchor: هذا نهي جامع عن ملابسة شيء مما يأمره به المشركون . والمقصود من النهي تأسيس قاعدة لأعمال الرسول والمسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.claim: The indefinite ‘whoever’ can apply generally to anyone matching the description; another report says the verse concerned Umayya ibn Khalaf asking that poor Muslims be expelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r2.anchor: وما صدق ( من ) كل من اتصف بالصلة ، وقيل نزلت في أمية بن خلف الجمحي ، دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى طرد فقراء المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.claim: Making a heart heedless means its constitution leaves it inattentive to divine unity so polytheism takes root; these people have weak insight and are driven by habit and desire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r3.anchor: والمراد بإغفال القلب جعله غافلا عن الفكر في الوحدانية حتى راج فيه الإشراك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.claim: The persistent heedlessness is innate, while following desire is a chosen act; the two clauses distinguish created disposition from human agency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r4.anchor: فالغفلة خلقة في قلوبهم ، واتباع الهوى كسب من قدرتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.claim: Furaṭ means injustice and aggression, derived from going ahead because wrongdoing rushes into evil; amr means condition, and kāna marks its entrenched state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p307/r5.anchor: والفرط بضمتين : الظلم والاعتداء . وهو مشتق من الفروط وهو السبق لأن الظلم سبق في الشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.claim: Meccan leaders, or alternatively Uyayna b. Hisn and his party, asked Muhammad to dismiss poor believers such as Ammar, Suhayb, Salman, Ibn Masud, and Bilal; Ibn Atiyya prefers the Meccan leaders because the sura is Meccan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r1.anchor: عظماء الكفار قيل من أهل مكة، وقيل عيينة بن حصن وأصحابه والأول أصوب، لأن السورة مكية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.claim: The leaders complained that the poor companions' clothes smelled and demanded their removal before they would sit with the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r2.anchor: يريدون عمار بن ياسر وصهيب بن سنان وسلمان الفارسي وابن مسعود وغيرهم من الفقراء كبلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.claim: Reports say the Prophet sat with the poor believers and praised God for commanding him to be patient with them, welcoming those for whom his Lord reproached him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r3.anchor: خرج إليهم وجلس بينهم، وقال الحمد لله الذي جعل من أمتي من أمرت أن أصبر نفسي معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.speaker: سلمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.claim: Salman reports that Uyayna, al-Aqra, and their companions, described as those whose hearts were reconciled, made the same demand, prompting the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r4.anchor: وروى سلمان أن المؤلفة قلوبهم، عيينة بن حصن والأقرع بن حابس وذويهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.claim: The report about the reconciled leaders could make the verse Medinan, but Ibn Atiyya thinks it was likely Meccan and a reply to Quraysh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r5.anchor: فالآية على هذا مدنية، ويشبه أن تكون الآية مكية، وفعل المؤلفة قريش فرد بالآية عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.claim: Here ṣbir means to hold or restrain oneself; the related term describes an animal held as a target, which the Prophet forbade.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r6.anchor: واصبر معناه احبس، ومنه المصبورة التي جاء فيها الحديث: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صبر الحيوان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.claim: The majority read al-ghadati; Ibn Amir and several early readers read al-ghudwati, despite the latter's grammatical weakness because ghudwa is a known proper noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r7.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «بالغداة» ، وقرأ ابن عامر «بالغدوة» وهي قراءة نصر بن عاصم ومالك بن دينار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.claim: The alif-lam in al-ghudwa can be explained as making the time word indefinite or generic, as in al-fina, so the reading has a possible defense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r8.anchor: وجه القراءة بذلك أنهم ألحقوها ضربا من التنكير إذ قالوا حيث غدوة يريدون الغدوات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.claim: The morning and evening invocation refers to the five daily prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r9.anchor: الإشارة بقوله يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي إلى الصلوات الخمس. قاله ابن عمر ومجاهد وإبراهيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.claim: The morning-and-evening invocation specifically means the dawn and afternoon prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة المراد صلاة الفجر، وصلاة العصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.claim: The verse also includes people who invoke God outside prayer and those who gather to study religious knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r1.anchor: ويدخل في الآية من يدعو في غير صلاة، ومن يجتمع لمذاكرة علم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet says remembering God morning and evening is better than breaking swords in God's path or freely giving wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r2.anchor: روى عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال «لذكر الله بالغداة والعشي أفضل من حطم السيوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman read al-ghudu without the final h; Ibn Abi Abla read the morning and evening terms as plurals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن «بالغدو» دون هاء، وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «بالغدوات» «والعشيات» على الجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.claim: Not turning one's eyes from the believers means not looking past them toward worldly people and the clothing of disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r4.anchor: أي لا تتجاوز عنهم إلى أبناء الدنيا والملابس من الكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p512#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
