TABRISI:18:28-29#3/r3.anchor: ترك الإيمان والاستدلال بآيات الله واتبع الهوى

THALABI:v6p165/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r12.claim: The verse was revealed when Uyayna ibn Hisn asked Muhammad to remove poor companions such as Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Amir ibn Fuhayra, Mihja, and Salman so nobles could follow him.
THALABI:v6p165/r12.anchor: نزلت في عيينة بن حصين الفزاري، وذلك أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v6p165/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p165/r13.claim: The command to be patient means keep company with those who worship and revere God at dawn and evening, seeking Him rather than worldly gain or display.
THALABI:v6p165/r13.anchor: واصبر: واحبس نفسك مع الذين يدعون: يعبدون ربهم ويوقرون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

THALABI:v6p165/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r14.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p165/r14.claim: Qatada interprets dawn and evening as the Fajr and Asr prayers.
THALABI:v6p165/r14.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني: صلاة الصبح والعصر

THALABI:v6p165/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r15.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v6p165/r15.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar swears they are the people who perform the obligatory prayers.
THALABI:v6p165/r15.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفسي بيده إنهم لأهل الصلوات المكتوبة

THALABI:v6p165/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p165/r16.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p165/r16.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns the seven hundred poor men of the Suffa who stayed at the Prophet's mosque, praying and waiting for the next prayer.
THALABI:v6p165/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب الصفة، وكانوا سبعمائة رجل فقراء

THALABI:v6p166/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p166/r1.claim: After the verse came down, the Prophet thanked God for giving him people with whom he was commanded to be patient.
THALABI:v6p166/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v6p166/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r2.claim: The command not to turn one's eyes away means not to look toward leaders, wealthy people, or nobles seeking worldly adornment.
THALABI:v6p166/r2.anchor: ولا تعد عيناك: لا تصرف ولا تجاوز عيناك عنهم إلى غيرهم

THALABI:v6p166/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r3.claim: Another explanation places this gaze during the poor worshippers' seeking forgiveness and says the verse rebukes the Prophet for wanting worldly status.
THALABI:v6p166/r3.anchor: ومعنى الآية: ولا تعد عيناك عنهم- مريدا زينة الدنيا- حال خوضهم في الاستغفار

THALABI:v6p166/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r4.claim: Making a heart heedless means God left it and caused it to forget His remembrance.

THALABI:v6p166/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v6p166/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the person whose heart is heedless as Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.
THALABI:v6p166/r5.anchor: قال أبو العالية: يعني: أمية بن خلف الجمحي

THALABI:v6p166/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r6.claim: Another identification names Uyayna ibn Hisn.
THALABI:v6p166/r6.anchor: وقال غيره: يعني عيينة بن حصين

THALABI:v6p166/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r7.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد
THALABI:v6p166/r7.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid gloss faratan as waste or loss.

THALABI:v6p166/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p166/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses faratan as opposing the truth.

THALABI:v6p166/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r11.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v6p166/r11.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses faratan as excess.

THALABI:v6p166/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r12.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v6p166/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses faratan as exceeding the limit.

THALABI:v6p166/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r13.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v6p166/r13.claim: Al-Farra glosses faratan as abandoned or left behind.

THALABI:v6p166/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r14.claim: Another gloss is falsehood; Abu Zayd al-Balkhi takes it as having advanced into evil.
THALABI:v6p166/r14.anchor: وقيل: باطلا. وقال أبو زيد البلخي: قدما في الشر

THALABI:v6p166/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v6p166/r15.claim: Abu Ubayd relates faratan to a horse that outruns the other horses and speech that gets ahead of its speaker.
THALABI:v6p166/r15.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: هو من قول العرب: فرس فرط

THALABI:v6p166/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p166/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p166/r16.claim: The phrase also means that the person wasted his affairs and days; a believer uses time instead of being used by it.
THALABI:v6p166/r16.anchor: قالوا: ان المؤمن من يستعمل الأوقات، ولا تستعمله الأوقات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi refers readers to his fuller account of the occasion and variant reading under the passage in al-Anam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r1.anchor: مفسرا بما فيه من النزول، واختلاف القراءة في سورة الأنعام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.speaker: علي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r2.claim: “Do not let your eyes pass beyond them” means do not look past them to others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r3.claim: The command means do not repel them with one's gaze or regard for others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r4.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as “do not turn your eyes away from them.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says not to turn one's sight toward people of status and adornment; although the eyes are addressed, the Prophet is meant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r5.anchor: لا تصرف بصرك إلى غيرهم من ذوي الهيئات والزينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r6.claim: The worldly adornment sought here means company with high-status and wealthy people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.claim: “Wanting worldly adornment” is a circumstantial phrase: the Prophet is forbidden to leave poor believers while seeking elite company.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (قوله: {تريد} هاهنا في موضع الحال)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.claim: The Prophet sought chiefs' faith hoping their followers would follow; he was not accused of worldly desire, but was directed to give believers his attention and not incline toward elites. Compare the rebuke in Abasa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p598/r8.anchor: وكان -صلى الله عليه وسلم- حريصا على إيمان الرؤساء طمعا في إيمان أتباعهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.claim: “Do not obey the one whose heart We made heedless” refers to Uyaina and his father, who wanted the poor removed so they could sit with the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد عيينة وأباهه) (¬1)، أي: لا تطعهم في تنحية الفقراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.claim: “We made his heart heedless” can mean that God left him unmarked or found him heedless, like bare land or an unvowelled book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r2.anchor: من جعلناه غافلا. قال: ويكون في الكلام أغفلته سميته غافلا، ووجدته غافلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses “his affair was farat” as waste or loss.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r4.claim: Qatada says his affair was wasted in the greatest way.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r6.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes “farat” as an affair treated carelessly; al-Wahidi connects this with neglect and ruin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r7.claim: Al-Layth says “farat” is an affair left unattended.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.claim: Al-Farra explains “farat” as something left with obedience abandoned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r8.anchor: فرطا: متروكا قد ترك فيه الطاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas via Ata says the man overreached in his demand and sought rank with God without piety; “farat” can derive from excess beyond bounds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r9.anchor: يريد أنه أفرط في مسألته، وأحب أن يرتفع عند الله بغير تقوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.claim: Muqatil glosses the word as extravagance, which may mean the excessive demand described by Ibn Abbas or the neglect described by al-Kalbi and al-Farra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r10.anchor: نحو هذا روي عن مقاتل أنه قال في قوله: {فرطا} قال: (سرفا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi reports Uyaina's boast that he and his people were Mudar's chiefs and that everyone would follow if they submitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r11.anchor: قال الكلبي: (قال عيينة: إنا رؤوس مضر (¬5) وأشرافها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.claim: Al-Farra says Uyaina went too far by boasting that he was the Arabs' chief and they followed his religion, making his conduct excessive and boastful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: (إنه أفرط في القول فقال: نحن رؤوس مضر وأشرافها، # وليس كذلك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.speaker: أبو زيد البلخي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p600/r13.claim: Abu Zayd al-Balkhi explains “farat” as a prior evil deed, from something that has gone ahead or occurred.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.claim: The command to stay with those who pray morning and evening is explained in al-Anʿām; he must not turn toward high-status people seeking worldly adornment or obey those who want the poor removed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r4.anchor: مفسر في سورة الأنعام إلى قوله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.claim: The person whose heart God made heedless abandoned faith and reflection on God's signs, following desire in a wasted and ruinous affair.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:26-28/r5.anchor: وكان أمره فرطا } أي: ضياعا هلاكا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the morning and evening remembrance with the dawn and afternoon prayers; the prescribed prayers began a year before the Prophet left Mecca for Medina.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r1.anchor: قوله: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} [الكهف: 28] قال قتادة: وهما الصلاتان: صلاة الفجر وصلاة العصر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.claim: The verse was revealed when the polytheists demanded that the Prophet dismiss Salman, Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Salim before they would sit with him; it links to a similar command.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r2.anchor: نزلت في سلمان الفارسي، وبلال، وصهيب، وخباب بن الأرت، وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.claim: Muʿāwiya b. Qurra interprets the command to remain with those who call on God morning and evening as referring to prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r3.anchor: الخليل بن مرة قال: سمعت معاوية بن قرة يقول في هذه الآية: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} [الكهف: 28] ، قال: في الصلاة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.claim: The Prophet thanked God for placing in his community people with whom he was commanded to keep patient company.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r4.anchor: الحسن بن دينار، عن قتادة قال: لما نزلت: {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} [الكهف: 28] قال رسول الله: «الحمد لله الذي جعل في أمتي من أصبر نفسي معه»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.claim: The Prophet says remembrance morning and evening is better than the finest swords or freely given wealth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لذكر الله بالغداة والعشي أفضل من خطم السيوف في سبيل الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.claim: The Prophet tells Suraqa that keeping company with people remembering God from dawn prayer to sunrise is dearer than freeing four slaves.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r6.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.claim: The Prophet says sitting with people remembering God after the afternoon prayer until sunset is dearer than freeing eight descendants of Ishmael.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p181/r7.anchor: الربيع بن صبيح، عن يزيد الرقاشي، عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لأن أجالس قوما يذكرون الله بعد صلاة العصر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the heedless person's desire is his appetite, and Mujāhid and al-Suddī gloss his affair as waste; the phrase is linked to two verses about neglect.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p182/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه} [الكهف: 28] ، يعني: شهوته. تفسير السدي.

ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:27-31/r2.claim: Those who pray morning and evening are rendered as seeking their Lord's beauty; the Prophet is told not to turn his eyes away from them for worldly adornment.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.claim: Quraysh elites said they would meet the Prophet if he dismissed poor believers; the verse warns against adopting their attitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r1.anchor: Kureyş’in ileri gelen ailelerine mensup müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’in fakir müminlerle birlikte bulunmasından rahatsızlık duyduklarını, bu insanları yanından uzaklaştırması halinde kendisiyle görüşebileceklerini söylüyorlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.claim: Honor comes from faith and good character, not wealth; the Prophet should recite to all without favoring the rich, since God knows who benefits, and should remain earnestly with the poor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r2.anchor: Üstünlük ve şeref, dünya malında ve ziynetinde değil, gönül ziynetindedir, yani iman ve güzel ahlâktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.claim: The same warning appears in 6:52: do not drive away those who call on God morning and evening seeking His favor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:28/r3.anchor: Rablerinin rızâsını isteyerek sabah akşam O’na yalvaranları kovma!

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.speaker: خباب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.claim: The same report says the Prophet would leave the poor believers when he stood, after which the instruction to keep himself with those who call upon their Lord was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r2.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس معنا فاذا أراد أن يقوم قام وتركنا فنزل ﴿ واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم ﴾

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.speaker: خباب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.claim: The occasion for “keep yourself with those who call upon their Lord” was already given in the account from Khabbab in Surah al-An'am.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r1.anchor: تقدم سبب النزول في سورة الأنعام في حديث خباب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the instruction not to obey one whose heart is heedless concerned Umayya ibn Khalaf, who wanted the Prophet to expel the poor and favor Makkan leaders.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r2.anchor: نزلت في أمية بن خلف الجمحي وذلك أنه دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أمر كرهه الله من طرد الفقراء عنه وتقريب صناديد أهل مكة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.speaker: الربيع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the Prophet turned his attention to Umayya ibn Khalaf, who was inattentive to what he was being told, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r3.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تصدى لأمية بن خلف وهو ساه غافل عما يقال له فنزلت

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Uyayna ibn Hisn entered while Salman was with the Prophet and demanded that Salman be removed when Uyayna's party arrived; the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p144/r4.anchor: دخل عيينة بن حصن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده سلمان فقال عيينة إذا نحن أتيناك فأخرج هذا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.claim: Salmān reports that influential converts, including ʿUyayna and al-Aqraʿ, asked the Prophet to remove poor companions in coarse wool so they could sit near him and learn.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r1.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي، قال: جاء المؤلفة قلوبهم إلى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عيينة بن حصن والأقرع بن حابس

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.claim: After finding the poor companions remembering God at the back of the mosque, the Prophet praised God for commanding him to remain patient with them, saying life and death were with them.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r2.anchor: قال: "الحمد لله الذي لم يمتني حتى أمرني أن أصبر نفسي مع رجال من أمتي، معكم المحيا ومعكم الممات".

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the warning against obeying one heedless of God was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf, who urged the Prophet to expel the poor and favor Meccan nobles; heedlessness means a heart sealed from monotheism, and desire means polytheism.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p297/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا} قال: نزلت في أمية بن خلف الجمحي

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The next section resumes the surah's opening: after the cave story showed God helping those who serve His cause, the Prophet is told to keep reciting, direct guidance to poor companions, disregard wealthy opponents, and leave them their choice and fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the episode of the cave-dwellers was mentioned as a result of a question. It became evident from it that God does not let the efforts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Furutan means exceeding limits or oppressing; the Prophet's concern for wealthy leaders aimed to spread religion, but he risked neglecting devout companions to court them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: to exceed the limits and to oppress.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The stern address is not rebuke of the Prophet but of affluent, arrogant people who considered his companions inferior and demanded their exclusion before they would listen.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the harsh and stern tone of this verse is not directed at the Prophet (sws). It is, in fact, directed at the arrogant and the affluent

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r3.claim: One report, also attributed to Qatada, says the surah is Meccan except “Restrain yourself” (18:28).
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنها مكية إلا قوله تعالى ( واصبر نفسك ) الآية فمدني وروي ذلك عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r1.claim: Esoterically, the command to keep company with those who call on God means companionship with poor devotees; the Prophet’s company benefits them as the mirror and source of divine disclosure they behold.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r1.anchor: أمر بصحبة الفقراء الذين انقطعوا لخدمة مولاهم وفائدتها منه عليه الصلاة والسلام تعود عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r2.claim: For others, the benefit of companionship returns to the companion; the poor are a company whose associate is not wretched.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r2.anchor: وأما صحبة الفقراء بالنسبة إلى غيره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ففائدتها تعود إلى من صحبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r3.speaker: عمرو المكي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r3.claim: ʿAmr al-Makkī calls company with righteous, sincere poor people the life of Paradise, moving a companion between contentment and certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r3.anchor: وقال عمرو المكي صحبة الصالحين والفقراء الصادقين عيش أهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r4.speaker: أبو مدين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r4.claim: Abū Madyan’s poem urges keeping poor companions, humility, accepting a low place, attending, and speaking only when asked.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r4.anchor: ولأبي مدين من قصيدته المشهورة التي خمسها الشيخ محيي الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r5.claim: “The poor” means Sufi masters; poverty is praised when joined to righteousness, while poverty joined to corruption is condemned.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r5.anchor: وعني بهؤلاء السادة الصوفية وقد شاع إطلاق الفقراء عليهم لأن الغالب عليهم الفقر بالمعنى المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r6.claim: A mawqūf report from Ibn ʿUmar urges humility and sitting with the poor to escape pride; another report calls it humility and excellent striving.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r6.anchor: فعن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما موقوفا تواضعوا وجالسوا المساكين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r7.claim: Another narration urges loving and sitting with the poor; their company teaches gratitude and contentment and avoids flattery, though it is hard on the self and thus greatly rewarded.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r7.anchor: وفي رواية أحبوا الفقراء وجالسوهم ومن فوائد مجالستهم إن العبد يرى نعمة الله تعالى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r8.claim: Some read “be patient with yourself” rather than “remain with” as an allusion to the difficulty of such company; this applies to others, not the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p307/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى ذلك ولكن ذلك بالنسبة إلى غيره صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r1.speaker: بعض أهل الأسرار
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r1.claim: Some esoteric interpreters say “yourself,” not “your heart,” because the Prophet’s heart was with God; he was commanded to accompany the poor openly while God reserved his heart privately.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r1.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الأسرار إنما قيل واصبر نفسك دون واصبر قلبك لأن قلبه الشريف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r2.claim: “You desire worldly adornment” means seeking nobles and wealthy people; it is blameworthy to incline to them and humble oneself for their wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r2.anchor: أي تطلب مجالسة الأشراف والأغنياء وأصحاب الدنيا وهي مذمومة مع الميل إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r3.claim: A hadith says whoever humbles himself to a rich person for wealth loses two-thirds of his religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r3.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث من تذلل لغني لأجل غناه ذهب ثلثا دينه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r4.claim: The wealthy may burden poor companions with reproach, even through the mere act of keeping them company; al-Zamakhsharī quips that favors turn bitter with reproach.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r4.anchor: فانه قلما يسلم الغني من المن على جليسه الفقير ولو بمجرد المجالسة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r5.speaker: بعض الشعراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r5.claim: A poet describes leaving a companion who followed generosity with reproach, not out of hatred or boredom but to escape the reproach.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308/r5.anchor: لنا صاحب ما زال يتبع بره بمن وبذل المن بالبر لا يسوى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r1.claim: The warning against obeying the heedless originally addressed people seeking to expel the poor, but its wording applies generally to all matters driven by the lower self.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r1.anchor: وكانوا في القصة يريدون طرد الفقراء وعدم مجالسة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لهم لكن العبرة بعموم اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r2.speaker: أهل الإشارة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r2.claim: Esoterically, one must not obey a heedless, veiled person in anything driven by the lower self, including deference to that person.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p308#2/r2.anchor: فلا يطاع عند أهل الإشارة الغافل المحجوب في كل شيء فيه هوى النفس وعدوا من إطاعته التواضع له

MAJAZ:v1p398/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p398/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p398/r3.claim: ملتحدا means a refuge or place to turn aside; it shares its root with اللحد and الإلحاد.
MAJAZ:v1p398/r3.anchor: «ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا» (28) أي معدلا واللحد منه والإلحاد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمحروفالزوائد)#748/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمحروفالزوائد)#748/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمحروفالزوائد)#748/r1.claim: The initial hamza in أَغْفَلْنَا is augmentative: Sībawayh says hamza is added at the start of verbs, as in أذهب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمحروفالزوائد)#748/r1.anchor: فالهمزة تزاد إذا كانت أول حرف في الاسم رابعة فصاعدا

BAQILLANI:v1p21/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r1.claim: Had the opponents been able to answer the challenge, they would have weakened the Prophet's claim and scattered his followers; their failure despite ample time proves they could not match or undermine the Qur'an.
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r1.anchor: فلما لم يفعلوا شيئا من ذلك مع طول المدة ووقوع الفسحة

BAQILLANI:v1p21/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r2.claim: The Qur'an describes its opponents as contentious, supporting the claim that their silence was inability rather than lack of argumentative skill.
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r2.anchor: وقد أخبر الله تعالى عنهم أنهم

BAQILLANI:v1p21/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r3.claim: Their shifting claims that the Qur'an was imitable, ancient tales, forged magic, poetry, madness, fabrication, or sorcery show confusion and excuse-making in place of a successful counter-text.
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r3.anchor: إلى آيات كثيرة في نحو هذا تدل على أنهم كانوا متحيرين في أمرهم متعجبين من عجزهم

BAQILLANI:v1p21/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r4.claim: They waged war, severed kinship, risked their lives, and demanded signs and angels, all in an effort to defeat him by some means.
BAQILLANI:v1p21/r4.anchor: وقد علم منهم أنهم ناصبوه الحرب وجاهدوه ونابذوه وقطعوا الأرحام وأخطروا بأنفسهم

KHATTABI:v1p24/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p24/r1.claim: The Qur'anic challenge to produce any sura like it, without specifying a particular sura, shows that the explanation under review misses the point of inimitability.
KHATTABI:v1p24/r1.anchor: فقال: {فاتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين} من غير تعيين

KHATTABI:v1p24/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p24/r2.speaker: علماء أهل النظر
KHATTABI:v1p24/r2.claim: Most speculative scholars attribute the Qur'an's inimitability to its eloquence, but cannot explain precisely how it differs from other eloquent speech.
KHATTABI:v1p24/r2.anchor: وزعم آخرون أن إعجازه من جهة البلاغة , وهم الأكثرون من علماء أهل النظر

KHATTABI:v1p24/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p24/r3.speaker: عامة أهل هذه المقالة
KHATTABI:v1p24/r3.claim: They say eloquence cannot be defined objectively; experts recognize its ranks by hearing, even when the cause of a speech's sweetness and liveliness is unclear.
KHATTABI:v1p24/r3.anchor: قالوا إنه لا يمكننا تصويره ولا تحديده بأمر ظاهر نعلم به مباينة القرآن غيره من الكلام

KHATTABI:v1p24/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p24/r4.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī rejects this appeal to an undefined impression as unconvincing, saying it merely turns a problem into ambiguity and leaves ignorance untreated.
KHATTABI:v1p24/r4.anchor: قلت: وهذا لا يقنع في مثل هذا العلم , ولا يشفى من داء الجهل به

KHATTABI:v1p24/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p24/r5.speaker: الرواة
KHATTABI:v1p24/r5.claim: Narrators say Jarīr met Dhū al-Rumma after he composed a poem, offered to add lines, and supplied a couplet praising the great houses of Tamīm.
KHATTABI:v1p24/r5.anchor: ذكرت الرواة أن جريرا مر بذي الرمة وقد عمل قصيدته التي أولها
